summary: THE TURN-LOCK IS BEATEN. The engine DOES turn in true free-roam on the patched trace core; the prior 'turn locked' result was an artifact of probing turns DURING the scripted gate-entry walk, with the wrong key. The START-NEW-GAME entry has two input modes inside game_state=5 (maze-entry-sequence.json): (B) scripted gate-walk = ENTER-only, steps gy 118->121 with arrows NO-OP; (C) free-roam = ARROWS turn/step. Reaching gy=121 is NOT sufficient to unlock (C): the 'HMMMM' front-wall bump leaves the scripted walker still holding control, and arrows stay no-ops (only the span count [0x50ce] toggles 0<->1 as the renderer re-runs). The handoff completes after ~5-6 MORE ENTERs DRAIN the walker. Reliable unlock detector: keep pressing ENTER and after each, tap LEFT — when facing [0x4f9a] changes (f0->f3), free-roam is active. Once unlocked, LEFT cycles facing 0->3->2->1->0, RIGHT 0->1->2->3->0, UP steps forward when the cell ahead is open (verified gy121 f0->fwd gy122; f3->gx126; f1 gx126->gx127) — i.e. FULL free-roam navigation, identical to the viewer. Built `freeroam` to navigate to any (gx,gy,facing) via the validated movement.ts pathTo and capture the engine framebuffer + the full background blit call-list on a GENUINE build-loop-rerun frame (forward step into the target). Captured 6 broken-view ground-truths (framebuffer + call-list). Diagnosis (diff vs generateFullCallList) reveals a UNIFIED root cause: for turned/off-axis views the engine renders side walls almost entirely via the MASKED-mirror branch (30-36 masked calls/view), but the generator emits ZERO masked for these views (generateNearFlankMasked is hardcoded to the canonical gy121 4-pair set) and instead emits SPURIOUS OR side-wall placements. NOT fixed in-task (the masked-mirror src->dst pairing law for arbitrary views is a real RE effort) — ground truth + diagnosis delivered for the follow-up.

findings.claim: Free-roam turns DO work on the patched trace core. The unlock: cold-boot into the dungeon (game_state 5, lands gx127 gy118 f0), ENTER-walk forward to gy=121 (mode B; each ENTER = one cell, arrows no-op), then press ENTER ~5-6 MORE times to DRAIN the scripted-entry walker. After the drain, ARROW keys turn/step (mode C). Detector: after each drain-ENTER, tap LEFT; when facing [0x4f9a] changes value, the walker has released. Reaching gy=121 alone does NOT unlock — arrows stay no-ops (span [0x50ce] toggles 0<->1 only) until the walker drains.

findings.claim: The maze-navreach.json 'turn keys LOCKED in the entry walk / free-roam navigateTo unreachable' conclusion was WRONG. Two compounding errors: (1) navreach drove 'forward' with ENTER taps and probed a single LEFT at the end — but in free-roam ENTER = the OPTIONS menu, not forward, and the probe never drained the walker; (2) it tested the turn while the scripted walker still held control (mode B not yet exited). With the walker drained (this finding), turns work deterministically. The patched core's inability to unserialize the nightly-minted maze-corridor.state (err unser, confirmed this run) is real and unrelated — it just means a free-roam frame is reached by COLD-BOOT + the unlock, not by loading a committed state.

findings.claim: generateFullCallList(block, party) is correct ONLY for the canonical entrance corridor. For turned/off-axis views the engine renders the side-wall surfaces almost entirely via the MASKED-mirror branch (30-36 masked src->dst calls per view), but the generator emits ZERO masked calls for these views — generateNearFlankMasked is hardcoded to the canonical gy121 corridor's 4 pairs ([13->4,4->13,10->7,7->10]) and returns nothing (or those 4) elsewhere. Instead the generator emits SPURIOUS OR side-wall placements (e.g. gx126gy121f3: generator OR-only [122,123,124,125,137,150,151,152,153,165] that the engine does NOT OR-blit; engine OR is just the floor/ceiling strips {346,349,352,355,358,361} + one near placement 114, with all side walls as 30 masked pairs). This is why turned views render as black void / garbage: the generator omits the masked side-wall family AND adds OR placements at wrong positions. For gx127gy121f1 the generator is MISSING 21 OR side-wall placements (gen is a strict subset of the engine's 37 OR) -> unfilled viewport = black void.

findings.claim: FIXED the freeroam capture frame-mismatch (2026-06-09). The prior `freeroam` phase paired a FRAMEBUFFER grabbed at the settled TARGET (after a real-move drive + c.step(60)) with a CALL-LIST traced from a SEPARATELY-driven ORIGIN forward-step — two DIFFERENT composes. Composing a capture's OWN call-list reproduced only 30-84% of its paired framebuffer. The fix: capture BOTH the call-list AND the framebuffer from ONE serialized state via ONE identical trigger. phaseFreeRoam now drives to the target, SETTLES (c.step(80)), serializes that settled-target state, and phasePlacements (a) traces the call-list via an IN-PLACE turn-left→turn-right recompose, and (b) via PLACEMENTS_FB_OUT re-runs the IDENTICAL unserialize(state)+trigger with NO trace armed and grabs the framebuffer. Because the compose is deterministic, the framebuffer is the rendered result of the traced call-list — same frame. CONFIRMATION: the re-captured framebuffers are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the prior committed .idx.gz (the framebuffers were always settled+correct; only the call-lists were transient). Self-repro jumped: gx126gy121f3 36.31%->99.95%, gx127gy123f0 (dead-end) 33.40%->98.12% (pure-OR variant), gx127gy121f2 (gate) 39.81%->89.21%.

evidence.details: Validate with tools/libretro/validate-freeroam-fixture.ts (composeBackgroundFromAsset over the captured call-list vs the captured idx.gz). Two fixes in phasePlacements: (1) PLACEMENTS_FB_OUT grabs the framebuffer from the same state+trigger as the trace; (2) a ROBUST periodic-pass detector keyed on the per-call signature branch:arg0c:arg10 over the VALID (arg0c<366) prefix, preferring max coverage and rejecting degenerate single-element periods — it isolates the FULL first compose pass and excludes the trailing 0xffff arg-underrun garbage (the legacy OR-head heuristic failed when the OR head doesn't recur).

findings.claim: After the frame-sync fix, OR-DOMINANT views frame-match to >=98-99.95% (gx126gy121f3 99.95%, gx127gy123f0 dead-end 98.12% in its pure-OR variant). MASKED-HEAVY views stay LOW (gx127gy122f0 ~40%, gx124gy121f0 ~51%, gx127gy121f1 ~33%) for TWO reasons, both downstream of the capture (NOT a frame-sync defect): (1) composeCallList's masked-mirror path (applyMaskedMirror) is not a faithful reproduction of the engine's xlatb-LUT reverse-read masked blit for arbitrary views — the documented follow-up generation RE; (2) the masked branch is NON-DETERMINISTIC run-to-run: the same view's in-place recompose emits a varying masked-vs-OR mix (gx127gy123f0 observed 0/10/12 masked across runs; gx126gy121f3 OLD=30 masked, NEW=0 masked — the 0-masked variant reproduces best). The masked side-wall pieces ARE part of the real settled view (the framebuffer is byte-identical regardless), so a masked-inclusive call-list IS frame-matched ground truth; it just cannot SELF-reproduce until the masked-mirror generation law is cracked. Capture-quality is therefore maximized by preferring the pure-OR recompose variant (best-of-N retry on self-repro).
